beats.say: The Moon is spinning right now. So why do we only ever see one side?
Most people think it doesn't rotate at all.
But it does. It turns once every 27 days, exactly as long as one trip around Earth.
Long ago, Earth's gravity pulled the Moon slightly out of shape and slowed its spin until the two matched.
And the far side isn't dark. It gets just as much sunlight. We first saw it in 1959, from a Soviet probe.
It's also drifting away from us, about four centimetres every year. Follow for more.

facts: The Moon turns once on its axis in about 27 days, the same time as one orbit of Earth
Earth's gravity raised a bulge on the Moon and slowed its spin until it matched the orbit
The far side gets about as much sunlight as the near side
The far side was first photographed in 1959 by the Soviet probe Luna 3
The Moon is moving away from Earth by about 3.8 cm a year
